references_named: W. H. Mallock, A Human Document (1892)
rationale: The mechanism genuinely enacts the idea: suppressing the native highlight and repurposing selectionchange to invert the usual keep/drop logic is exactly the kind of medium-as-argument move the DNA prizes. The source passage is well-chosen — a connoisseur, a price as rumour, an expensive belief — landing squarely on the P6 value/authenticity axis while leaving the reader's carving as pure chance (P5). Restraint is exemplary: one span per word, one event handler, no libraries, per-visit ground hue, no storage, no network, CC BY-SA stated. The double-coding works at both depths (Phillips's treatment, the death of the author, the web's unsaved authorship).
reservations: The reference to Phillips is precise and the mechanism is genuinely web-native, but the work sits in a crowded neighbourhood of selection-as-medium pieces in the broader net.art tradition; novelty is real but not radical. The 'death of the author' reading is gestured at rather than sharpened — a slightly more pointed source passage or a single line of wall text could deepen the P7 double-coding without breaking the surface gag.
revision_suggestion: Consider tightening the source passage so the surviving-poem potential is more legible on first encounter (e.g., a passage with stronger latent aphorisms), and add a one-line console attestation of the per-visit ground hue so the 'never the same twice' claim is materially attested rather than only visible.
